text: While loops keep repeating as long as their condition stays true — perfect when you don't know the count in advance.
We start count at zero, and bump it up by one each pass with the plus-equals shortcut.
The loop stops the instant count reaches five, [sniff] because then the condition becomes false.
One warning — if the condition never becomes false, you get an infinite loop that runs forever.
This second example simulates reading input over and over until the user finally types quit.
Sometimes you want to bail out early — break exits the loop immediately, even a while True infinite loop.
[cough] Continue is the opposite — it skips just the rest of this pass and jumps ahead to the next iteration.
Here continue skips the even numbers, so only the odds ever get printed.
[chuckle] And a lesser-known trick — while loops support an else clause that runs only if the loop finished naturally, without a break.
